items.title: Flip Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: he was the first guy that influenced me, that made something with me.

ctx.x: When you were first learning the tenor, did you have someone you wanted to sound like at that time? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

Well I played alto before the tenor, and the first guy I ever listed to was Frankie Trumbauer. That was in 1927. He made that record at Vic’s, “Singing the Blues” and I heard him play that and I says wow, he is good, he knows how to play the intervals you know. He was wonderful. And that’s the first guy I ever heard. Then I heard everybody else, but he was the first guy that influenced me, that made something with me. In those days they had Andy Sannella and Rudy Wiedoft and different saxophone players, but this…
Wasn’t there, some of those guys were almost doing like this semi-classical saxophone, like Rudy—
